newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. ambassador to France has brain haemorrhage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ambassador to France has brain haemorrhage.

text.p: U.S. ambassador to France Pamela Harriman was in serious condition in the American Hospital of Paris on Tuesday after suffering a brain haemorrhage on Monday evening, the U.S. embassy said.
Harriman, 76, a close supporter of President Bill Clinton, was taken ill at the Ritz Hotel where she had gone for a swim and she was taken to hospital by ambulance.

"The initial diagonisis is that the ambassador suffered a cerebral haemorrhage. She remains in serious condition," embassy spokesman Christopher Snow said in a brief statement read to reporters outside the hospital in the suburb of Neuilly.
A haemorrhage can cause paralysis or death by blocking the blood supply to the brain.
U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Harriman had "fainted and fell ill".
Her son, Winston Spencer Churchill, a British member of parliament and grandchild of the wartime British prime minister, was at her bedside, he added.
CNN quoted a senior administration official as saying Harriman was unconscious and "very close to death".

U.S. newspapers reported last year that Harriman wanted to leave Paris but she issued a statement denying any move was imminent and saying she would follow Clinton's wishes. Diplomatic sources said she had been expected to retire in June.

Harriman, whose full name is Pamela Digby Churchill Hayward Harriman, was born in Farnborough, England, and became a naturalised U.S. citizen after marrying her third husband, the late multimillionaire and diplomat Averell Harriman in 1971.
She was just 19 when she married Randolph Churchill, son of British prime minister Winston Churchill, during World War Two. They divorced as the war ended but the marriage produced her only child.
Her second marriage was to cinema magnate Leyland Hayward in 1960.
Harriman, a key Democratic fundraiser, was national co-chairman of the 1992 Clinton-Gore presidential campaign.
After Clinton was elected that year, one of his first stops was to attend a dinner party at Harriman's smart home in the Washington suburb of Georgetown.
For her favours to his party, Clinton named her ambassador to France in 1993, one of the most sought after diplomatic appointment.
